title: 1980s Nostalgic Summer Vacation
description: An incredibly detailed documentary-style prompt for Seedance 2.5 to recreate a nostalgic 1985 Japanese summer day through a home video lens.
promptText:
[Overview] A day in the life of a 10-year-old boy spending his summer vacation at his grandparents' rural home in 1985. A young uncle visiting home records with a handheld video camera from a distance without speaking. 480p, 16:9, 15 seconds. 7 shots (approx. 2s each) with hard cuts; all 7 locations are different. No transitions or fades. The subject does nothing for the camera: no eye contact, no showing objects, no waving, no posing. Immersed in play. Fragments cut from the middle of daily life, not acting. No dialogue, lines, or narration.

[Subject] Definition of beauty: A Japanese boy of child-actor caliber whom everyone says will be handsome in the future. A child's face the moment they enter water is best. Face: short black hair with bedhead, thick eyebrows, sharp double-lidded eyes, peeling skin on the bridge of the nose from sunburn (realistic skin texture), white teeth, a small scab on the chin. Clothing (everyday wear): white tank top (slightly yellowed from washing), green shorts, straw hat (frayed brim), white towel around the neck, bare feet in rubber sandals. Habits: pushing the hat back, glancing at the younger brother. Face, hair, and clothing are identical in all shots.

[Characters] Younger brother (6 years old): round face, buzzed head, white tank top and red shorts. Mimics everything the older brother does. Easily scared. No one looks at the camera.

[Era, Place, Light] Rural countryside in August 1985. 1) Veranda of an old Japanese house (morning light, thin smoke from a green coil mosquito repellent, rice with raw egg) 2) Rice field path (midsummer white light, bicycle) 3) Shallow river (sparkling water surface) 4) River rocks (jumping from a small rock to the shallows) 5) On a riverbank stone (watermelon, strong sunlight) 6) Tree in a shrine precinct (dappled sunlight, cicadas) 7) Veranda in the evening (sparkler firework: a small ball of fire sparking at the end of a thin paper twist. Blue twilight). No signs or text in the frame.

[Camera] 1985 home video camera texture: bleeding colors, low resolution, blown-out highlights on water reflections, soft outlines. No date display. Handheld, natural shake, imperfect composition, hunting zoom, exposure fluctuations. 3-6m distance from subject. Subject ignores the camera. No stabilization, gimbals, drones, slow motion, cinematic lighting, or commercial color grading. The camera is always at the height of a person holding it (standing, sitting, crouching, walking, next seat). No angles from places a person couldn't be. The filmer is a person clearly in the same space, following slightly late when the subject moves, occasionally with soft framing.

[Shots] (Approx. 2s each. Each line = Location & Light / Activity / Inner emotion and small leaked gestures / Camera position)
1. Veranda/Morning. Hurriedly eating rice with egg. Eyes already on the garden ahead. Emotion: Wanting to get to the river fast. Mosquito coil smoke drifts sideways. Camera: From outside the veranda.
2. Path/Bicycle. Standing to pedal with the brother on the back. Mouth set in a firm line looking ahead. Emotion: Reliable older brother vibe. Hat slips back in the wind. Camera: Following from behind, shaking.
3. Shallows. Submerged to the waist with a net, holding breath staring at fish. Emotion: Concentration. Brother still behind. Camera: From the bank, water reflections blown out.
4. Rocks. Diving from a small rock into the shallows, laughing loudly with face rising from splashing water. Emotion: Sense of liberation, refreshment. Camera: Slightly away from the bank, spray hits the screen.
5. Bank stone/Watermelon. Biting in, spitting seeds far, glancing at the brother with a smirk. Emotion: Competitiveness. Camera: From the side, strong sunlight.
6. Shrine tree/Dappled light. Thrusting a cicada caught in a net in front of the brother, laughing at him recoil. Emotion: Mischievousness. Camera: From behind the brother.
7. Veranda/Evening. Staring seriously at the fire ball of a sparkler, watching the spot it vanished after falling. Emotion: Small loneliness at the end of the day. Camera: Sitting at the edge of the veranda from the side. During this, at approx 00:14, the recording suddenly blacks out. No fade out.

[Prop Details] Net has a bamboo handle with green mesh. Bicycle is a black utility bike with a carrier. Straw hat brim is frayed. Watermelon is striped, eaten close to the rind. Mosquito coil is a green spiral in a ceramic pig holder. Sparkler has red paper at the tip of the twist.

[Prohibition of Text] No readable text, logos, signs, labels, or numbers on screen.

[Physics & Consistency] Real-world physics. No extra fingers, fused hands, distorted anatomy, floating objects, vanishing items, or sudden deformations. Splashes, wet hair/clothes, and sparks should be realistic. Feet grounded. Hat, towel, and brother's clothes same in all shots.

[Sound] Only natural ambient sounds (switches per shot): clinking of a rice bowl, bicycle chain and wind, river flow, splash of diving, biting watermelon, cicada chorus, crackling of sparklers. No words. Occasional small laughter/breaths from the filmer and subject allowed. No music, no narration, no artificial sound effects.

[Atmosphere] A record of a nondescript day of a boy in Showa-era countryside that makes adults feel 'I had a summer like this.' Fragments of play, not acting. Nostalgic, bright, deeply human. Prioritize the feeling that a camera just happened to be there.

She pushes loose hair away with the back of her wrist and briefly checks herself on the phone screen. The OPEN white La Mer jar casually enters the lower-left beside her cheek. Natural autofocus shift between face and jar. She exhales softly. Dialogue: “Okay. Last thing, then bed.” SHOT 2 — 0:04–0:07 Horizontal detail shot. Jar on the left, softly blurred part of her face on the right. She gently presses one fingertip into the thick white cream. Show realistic deformation: dense, silky, opaque cream folds under the finger and forms a soft peak when lifted. Briefly show the front label clearly: “CRÈME DE LA MER™” “LA MER” “moisturizing cream” Then she rubs a small amount between two fingertips. Natural rack focus: label → cream → fingertips. Dialogue: “It’s so rich.” SHOT 3 — 0:07–0:11 Return to horizontal face close-up. Her face slightly left-of-center, applying hand on the right. She warms the cream and gently presses small amounts onto both cheeks, forehead and chin. Do not create a thick white mask. The cream appears briefly, then gradually absorbs. Freckles, pores, under-eye shadows and fine skin texture remain visible. Only a subtle hydrated sheen develops. Dialogue: “I just warm it up and press it in.” SHOT 4 — 0:11–0:15 Closest three-quarter selfie framing. She presses two fingertips into her cheek, lifts them, then slowly turns into the warm sunlight. A subtle hydrated sheen catches the cheekbone while freckles and pores remain visible. She looks mostly at her phone screen, gives a tiny delayed half-smile and small nod. The white La Mer jar appears naturally in soft focus near the lower frame. She reaches toward the phone to stop recording, causing a slight natural sideways tilt. Dialogue: “Morning me is gonna be so happy.” PERFORMANCE End-of-day energy: relaxed, slightly tired, casual and natural. Include subtle micro-behaviors: slow blinking, small exhale, natural swallowing, tiny head tilt, eyes checking the screen, loose hairs falling across her cheek, small posture shifts, delayed half-smile. VOICE Soft female voice, slightly tired and flat. Close smartphone microphone sound. Natural breathing. No studio-clean voice-over. SKIN REALISM Pore-level realism. Visible freckles, pores, fine forehead texture, faint under-eye shadows, tiny imperfections, vellus facial hair, moist eyes, natural catchlights, real lip texture. The moisturizer must behave like a real thick cream before absorbing. No plastic skin, beauty-filter smoothing, artificial glow or waxy face. STRICT NEGATIVE No face drift. No character replacement. No hairstyle or outfit change. No packaging change. No blue jar, blue lid, blue cream or translucent gel. No Laneige or other skincare product. No product duplication. No fake label. title: Alien Planet Found-Footage Vlog
description: A found-footage style prompt of a woman exploring an alien coast, featuring on-camera lines and raw, atmospheric visuals.
promptText: [STYLE + CAMERA + ATMOSPHERE] Real found-footage phone vlog on an alien planet. She is filming as she walks, the way someone records a trip for a friend: uneven clips, hard cuts, the phone too close, then swung out at whatever just moved. Slight shake, bad exposure, soft focus, lens dirt, wind slamming the mic, then creatures and plants filling the frame. When she speaks to the lens, she says the exact short lines written below, clear and plain, in a normal speaking voice. Wind can sit under the words. It does not replace them. No transitions, no slow-mo, no grade, no text, no stickers. It feels raw because the planet is doing too much for a phone. A giant moon hangs in the sky the whole day, pale and huge, even with the suns up. [SUBJECT] A woman about 27 in alien years, off-world traveler filming her own vlog. Cool lilac-grey complexion, faint mint freckles, a short glassy hair-crest messy from wind, gold eyes. Simple field clothes the whole take: dusty linen wrap, travel shirt, boots, a small pack. Fully clothed in every clip. She talks to the lens only at the beats marked below, then forgets the camera and points it at the planet. Same face in every cut. Calm, curious, a little worn. Not performing. [PLACE] An alien wild coast, lived-in and too big for the phone. Chalk shelves, forests of tall ribbed plants that lean and creak, ground-cover that pulls back when a boot lands, a gel-river the color of bottle glass, herds crossing open amber flats, a cliff path under the giant moon. Two small suns. Wind, grit, insect-choir, distant animal calls. No postcard town. The extraordinary stuff is just outside the lane. [ON-CAMERA LINES] She only speaks these lines, in this order, in a clear everyday voice: 1. “Day two. That moon still hasn’t moved.” 2. “It’s fine. It’s just eating.” 3. “They cross here every day. Look at the legs.” 4. “Yeah. I’m not going in.” 5. “Two suns. Moon’s still up.” 6. “Stopping here. I’ll send this later.” [TIMELINE — PHONE VLOG, HARD CUTS] 0-4s: HOOK — she is already walking a chalk shelf, phone in her hand, giant moon filling the upper frame behind her. She turns the lens on herself and says, clear: “Day two. That moon still hasn’t moved.” Then she flips the phone out: a stand of ribbed plants as tall as towers, swaying, seed-pods knocking. Raw, immediate. 4-9s: She pushes through a lane of vegetation. Leaves the size of doors fold aside and settle behind her. Cut to the phone dropped low: ground-cover peeling back from her boots, pale roots clicking. Cut to her stopping, holding the phone steady, filming a slow six-legged grazer the size of a cart chewing a pod. It looks at the lens. She does not get closer. She says, clear, off the side of the frame: “It’s fine. It’s just eating.” Wind under the line, words intact. 9-15s: She crests a rise. The giant moon sits on the horizon, enormous, craters readable. She films it, then the phone dips and catches a herd of long-necked grazers crossing the amber flat, legs too many, moving like a slow traffic jam. Cut to a close of a plant opening as the herd passes, then shutting. Cut to her face for a second, squinting. She says, clear: “They cross here every day. Look at the legs.” Then the phone goes back to the animals. Overexposed, dusty, real. 15-21s: Gel-river. She stands on the bank and films the surface beading and rolling upstream. Something large moves under it, a dark shape, then a fin of shell breaks and sinks. She steps back, laughs once, and says, clear: “Yeah. I’m not going in.” Cut to her crouched, filming a cluster of cube-bodied river birds pecking the mud. One hops onto a rock and stares. She stays quiet. Cut to the moon reflected, broken, in the gel. Phone almost slips. She catches it. 21-26s: Afternoon wind. She follows a dirt track between breathing shell-boulders. A door-sized beetle crosses ahead and she waits, filming its legs, then its eye, then the plants it brushes. She stays quiet. Cut to her wiping the lens with her sleeve. Cut to a high shelf: two suns, the giant moon still up, a valley of moving forest below. She turns the lens on herself and says, clear: “Two suns. Moon’s still up.” Then she holds the wide shot. The audio is wind, the far call, and that line. 26-30s: The light drops. The moon brightens until it is the main light. She films a night-opening grove, pods glowing faint mint, small flyers stitching between them. Cut to her face, tired, hair-crest flat from the wind, the moon over her shoulder. She says, clear: “Stopping here. I’ll send this later.” Last shot: phone pointed out from the shelf at the giant moon and the dark gel-river, a herd still moving as small shapes, her breathing on the mic, then the recording ends mid-step, like a real vlog file. [REALISM LOCK] Found footage alien vlog only. Handheld phone, hard cuts, dirty lens, wind, bad exposure. Same woman, fully clothed, same face. She speaks only the six written lines, in order, intelligible, everyday English. Giant moon in the sky all day. Creatures and vegetation carry the clips: ribbed forest, ground-cover that pulls back, a six-legged grazer, a many-legged herd, cube-bodied river birds, a shape under the gel, a door-sized beetle. Raw, specific, extraordinary, and ordinary to her.

title: K-Drama vs Reality Performance Contrast
description: A detailed cinematic video prompt for Seedance that contrasts the romanticized aesthetics of Korean dramas with the gritty, direct feel of a mobile phone recording using character binding.
promptText:
Duration: 20 seconds
Frame: 9:16 vertical screen
Theme: The contrast between the same Korean phrase in K-dramas vs. reality.
Format: Single character, dual states, five sets of A/B hard-cut comparisons.

[Character Binding]
Unique character card. Keep the same character identity throughout, using face, hairstyle, and clothing from the reference image without redesigning looks.
A and B are two performances by the same person, not a dialogue between two people, no dual-person framing or split screen.

[State A | Korean Romantic Movie]
Close-up of characters in a Korean romantic movie, refined, gentle, subtle, with a slight romantic feel.

Lighting:
Large soft light from the window side illuminates the face, with delicate light-shadow transitions; a beam of soft warm backlight from the side-rear gently outlines the hair and shoulder. Eyes have natural catchlights, face is three-dimensional, no flat beautifying light.

Color Grading:
Creamy white highlights, low-saturation warm skin tones, slight bluish-gray cool shadows. Overall clear, black levels slightly soft, smooth transition in bright areas. Background is biased towards off-white, light gray, and light warm colors.

Cinematic Texture:
Medium-telephoto portrait lens look, shallow depth of field, eyes and mouth clear, curtains and distant lights softened into delicate bokeh. High-intensity highlights with extremely slight soft halo, retaining skin texture and subtle film grain.
Each A shot has only a very slight, almost imperceptible slow zoom-in.

Performance:
Soft gaze, natural breathing, small range of movement. Short emotional pause before speaking, voice is soft, sentence ends fall lightly, like speaking to someone close in a K-drama.

[State B | Ordinary Mobile Phone Shot]
Reality indoor mobile front-facing direct shot, simple gray wall background, direct front lighting. Neutral white balance, contrast and sharpness more direct than A, background also clearer.
Cancel A's backlight contour, shallow DOF bokeh, soft halo, and cinematic grading, but maintain normal exposure and realistic skin texture.
Fixed camera, composition slightly tighter than A, retaining a slight mobile wide-angle close-range feel, no exaggerated facial stretching.

Performance:
Staring directly at the camera, eyes and eyebrows noticeably tense, body leaning slightly forward, tone short, direct, and impatient. Comedy comes from sudden face change and speaking style, not acting as an out-of-control scream.

[Composition & Editing]
Unified vertical medium close-up from head to waist, eye position kept at similar height.
Hard cut to B immediately after A finishes, texture, expression, and sound change simultaneously.
Same face remains recognizable at every cut, no distortion, white flashes, black frames, or costume changes.

SHOT 1 | 00–04s | Don't Look

Subject:
Same person, contrast between gentle subtlety and direct reprimand.

Action / Performance:
00–02s, State A:
Character looks down-side first, then gently turns eyes to camera with a hint of subtle smile, softly says 'Don't look'. Finishes and retracts gaze slightly, maintaining natural shyness.
Camera zooms in very slowly, soft warm backlight illuminating a small amount of hair.

02–04s, Hard cut State B:
Character stares directly at camera, brows tight, head slightly forward, repeats 'Don't look' with a significantly heavier tone, followed by an expletive.
Last word falls, gaze still fixed on camera, a hint of displeased stillness.

Dialogue:
A: '보지 마.'
B: '보지 마, 이 개새끼야.'

Environment / Camera / Style:
A features soft light curtains and creamy bokeh, K-drama cinematic texture.
B features gray wall, direct light, and fixed mobile shot.

Constraints:
Both phrases spoken by the person in frame, finish A then cut to B, accurate lip-sync.

(Remaining segments follow the same contrast pattern...)

title: Dark Gothic Psychological Horror Mirror Scene
description: A detailed narrative prompt for Seedance 2.5 depicting a psychological horror encounter between a jester and her reflection, with precise choreography and atmospheric details.
promptText: HALF A BEAT LATE — 15 seconds. Dark gothic psychological horror. 16:9. Real-time action, controlled cuts, continuous spatial and emotional progression. REFERENCES Image 1 defines adult female jester Sin and her identical evil mirror double: exact face, white makeup, red nose, dark eye makeup, painted tear marks, red twin-horn hair, gold crown with bells, ivory ruff, red-and-blue court costume, pointed shoes. Image 2 defines the room and opening frame: burgundy curtain and warm wall sconce on the left, charcoal walls, wooden floor, large antique gold mirror on the right. Preserve the room, mirror frame, and light direction. IDENTITY AND STAGING SIN starts outside the mirror: increasingly frightened, resisting capture. DOUBLE starts inside the mirror: amused, disobedient, smiling, physically assertive. After the exchange, DOUBLE is outside in the room and SIN is trapped behind intact glass. Begin on Image 2’s empty-room composition. Sin enters from lower-left, walks diagonally to the mirror, and stops about 55 cm from the glass, torso facing it, back and partial profile toward camera. Keep her slightly off the mirror center so both real and reflected faces stay visible. Camera remains on the mirror’s left-front side; the glass stays broadly visible, not edge-on. Natural perspective, readable facial detail, enough depth of field for both faces. During the exchange, Sin passes inward through the screen-left half of the mirror while Double steps outward through the screen-right half. Their paths stay separate. Afterward Double takes one short settling step toward screen-left, ending in the left foreground while trapped Sin remains visible inside the mirror on the right. PERFORMANCE LOCK Sin stops smiling once she notices the anomaly and never smiles again. Double keeps smiling and never copies Sin’s fear. Sin shakes her head, retreats, gasps, loses balance, resists. Double refuses to follow, advances, grips, pulls, plants its feet. After the exchange, Sin panics inside the mirror while Double turns toward camera, smiles wickedly, then whispers. Both faces stay alive and natural, never frozen or deformed. 0-3 SECONDS — THE SMILE REMAINS A heel clicks offscreen. Sin enters immediately, takes two or three short grounded steps to the mirror, relaxed posture, chin slightly raised, small habitual smile. Weight transfers naturally through each foot; skirt and crown bells follow with soft motion and sound. Her reflection appears normal at first. Sin briefly adjusts the side of her crown with her right hand, lowers it, exhales, and her mouth turns neutral. The reflected hand lowers about half a second late. Double keeps smiling and slowly shows its teeth. A restrained push-in keeps both faces readable: Sin neutral and unsmiling, Double still smiling. 3-5.5 SECONDS — OPEN DISOBEDIENCE Sin looks from Double’s mouth to its eyes, brow tightening, then slowly shakes her head once. Double does not shake. It tilts its head slightly and widens its amused smile. Sin catches her breath, draws her chin back, retreats about 20 cm, and raises her right hand at chest height, palm toward the mirror. Double leans closer to the glass as Sin increases her real distance. Keep both opposing movements visible in the same oblique frame. 5.5-8 SECONDS — GRIP, THEN PULL Hard cut to a same-side medium shot holding both faces, Sin’s raised right wrist, and the mirror’s left edge. A localized patch of glass turns into a dark elastic membrane. Double’s left hand reaches through into the room and grips Sin’s right wrist firmly. Double pulls inward. Sin’s eyes snap to the captured wrist; her lips part in a sharp inhale. Her left hand grabs the mirror’s left frame, rear foot braces on the wooden floor, knees bend as she pulls backward. Double keeps its cold smile and retracts with steady force. Sin loses her hold on the frame. Her right shoulder is pulled forward first, then her torso; her rear shoe begins to slide. She resists the whole time and never walks voluntarily into the mirror. 8-11.5 SECONDS — ONE IN, ONE OUT The camera withdraws slightly to reveal the mirror boundary and landing foot. Double steps outward through the screen-right half of the mirror and plants one pointed shoe firmly on the wooden floor before taking weight. Sin is pulled inward through the screen-left half. Double keeps hold until Sin crosses the surface, then releases her wrist. Their identical faces pass on separate paths: Sin terrified, trembling, ragged breath; Double composed with a small victorious smile. Red hair and moving fabric briefly occlude the crossing point. Use one concealed continuity cut inside that occlusion only. When the occlusion clears, the exchange is complete: inside the mirror Sin stumbles one step away, then turns and lunges back toward the glass; outside, Double completes its settling step toward screen-left. The membrane seals back into intact reflective glass before Sin reaches it. Her palms hit the inner surface and stop. The gold frame stays rigid. No shattering. 11.5-13 SECONDS — TURN FIRST Hard cut to a same-side medium close shot that clearly contains both faces. Double starts facing the mirror, then shoulders and torso turn toward the camera until its face is fully visible. Show the full body turn before any frontal smile. Behind it, trapped Sin faces outward from inside the mirror. She looks down at her blocked palms, urgently scans the frame edges, then looks at Double. She strikes the glass once and opens her mouth to call out, unheard. Sin remains an independent trapped person, not a synchronized reflection. 13-14 SECONDS — THEN THE EVIL SMILE Double finishes turning and stands still, shoulders relaxed, eyes on the lens. Only now does one corner of its mouth rise into a clearly wicked, satisfied smile with a little tooth visible. Keep Sin sharply readable behind it: raised inner brows, tense lower lids, downturned mouth, fast chest movement, palms pressed to the glass. Her fear continues throughout Double’s smile. 14-15 SECONDS — FINALLY, “SHH” Double raises its right index finger to its lips, slightly gathers its smile, and whispers directly to camera: “Shh.” The voice is low, intimate, steady. Sin strikes the glass again with one hand while the other stays planted, mouth open in a silent plea. She never mirrors the finger gesture, smile, or gaze. Hard cut to black at exactly 15 seconds. COLOR AND LIGHT Single consistent palette: charcoal brown #211E1B for walls and deep shadow, dark burgundy #4B171A for curtain and red costume shadow, aged brass #9C7544 for mirror frame, crown, and bells, ivory grey #D8D0C1 for makeup and ruff, deep blue-grey #29313B for blue costume fabric and cool shadow. Preserve Image 2’s warm left-side sconce at about 2700-3000K. Localized old-gold highlights, subtly cool shadows, neutral midtones, restrained saturation, dense textured blacks. Protect the white makeup from orange or blue contamination. Mirror glare never hides the reflected face. No color, exposure, or lighting reset during the exchange. AUDIO Heel clicks, fabric movement, and delicate bells establish the room. Sin’s interrupted breath builds into gasps during resistance. Add wrist-grip friction, shoe scrape, frame contact, and restrained membrane tension. After the mirror seals, Sin’s voice and breathing are inaudible from the room; her impacts become faint muffled thuds. Double’s final “Shh” is the only spoken line. No music, narration, or subtitles. CONTINUITY LOCKS Exactly one original Sin and one evil Double. Preserve separate identities, correct wrist ownership, grip contact, resistance, and inward/outward travel paths across cuts. No merged bodies, duplicate occupants, extra hands, or position jumps. Before the anomaly, the reflection behaves naturally. After the exchange, both performances remain independent. title: Korean Neighborhood Action-Comedy Scene
description: A detailed prompt for a comedy scene set in a Korean residential area, focusing on character consistency and a handheld camcorder aesthetic.
promptText:

The woman walks down a quiet residential street carrying a small grocery bag. She notices the man riding a tiny electric scooter toward her way too fast.
SHOT 2

SHOT 3

title: Woodland Alchemist Forest Video Storyboard

promptText:
Dawn in a wet old-growth forest, low mist between trunks. The small woodland alchemist crouches on a fallen log crusted with shelf fungus, hood of living stump and real mushrooms on her head. She scrapes the gills with one fingertip, then leans in until her face nearly touches it; the round jar-goggles flare green against the wet bark. Cold curiosity, total absorption, no smile. (2s)
- Night at a black forest stream, bioluminescent moss. Her field-assistant toad hops onto her open palm. She stops everything, turns the hand slowly to watch what the animal does, then writes it into the small notebook strapped to her specimen harness without taking her eyes off it. Working, not cuddling. (2s)
- Inside a hollow stump lit only by fungal glow. She raises a glass specimen jar against the light and rotates it, a fern root inside still faintly glowing. Her face hardens with attention rather than wonder, jaw set, eyes narrowing behind the green jar-goggles. (2s)
- Heavy rain hammering the forest floor. She does not run. She hunches her shoulders over the specimen jar, shields it with her whole body and keeps walking through the mud at the same unhurried pace, the mushrooms on her hood shivering under the drops. (2s)
- A clearing in raking afternoon light. She stops writing, reaches out and pulls a tick off the back of a small animal with a quick unceremonious pinch, flicks it away, and goes straight back to the notebook. Gentle, not sweet; the whole gesture takes a second. (2s)
- Neutral dark empty background, no environment. She is back in her signature look: living stump hood, mossy cloak, specimen harness. She walks two steps forward into the centre of frame, stops, lifts her chin and looks straight into the lens with a dry half-smile. The jar-goggles glow green, a rim light holds her silhouette and everything else falls to black. (3s)

title: 1986 Japanese Housing Complex Girl Video Prompt
description: A meticulous, long-form multi-sequence historical recreation prompt mapping a young girl's day in a 1986 Japanese suburban housing district.
promptText:
[Overview] In 1986, the day of an 8-year-old girl living in a public housing complex. Recorded by her mother from a distance using her father's video camera without speaking to her. 480p, 16:9, 15 seconds. 7 shots (approx. 2 seconds each) with hard cuts across 7 completely different locations. No transitions or fades. The subject does nothing facing the camera: no looks, no showing objects, no waving, no posing. Absorbed in play and tasks. Fragments cutting into raw daily life, not acting. No dialogue, speech, or narration at all.

[Subject] Standard of appearance: A Japanese girl cute enough to be a child actor, known as the prettiest in class. A focused face and a face that naturally smiles when successful are best. Face: cleanly cut bob hair (straight bangs), round face, large eyes with prominent black irises, a small upturned nose, red cheeks (realistic skin texture), one missing front tooth. Clothes (everyday wear): a white blouse with a round collar (slightly loose collar), a red jumper skirt, white high socks (one slipping down), white canvas shoes, a red pin on the left side of her hair. Behavioral habits: gazing at things she completed right in front of her face, pulling up her socks. Face, hair, and clothing are entirely consistent in all shots.

[Characters] 2 friends: a girl with a ponytail in a yellow T-shirt (freckles), a girl with braids in a light blue one-piece dress (glasses). None look at the camera.

[Era/Location/Light] A housing complex in the summer of 1986. (1) Balcony (among drying laundry, morning light) (2) Elastics jump game in the courtyard (two people stretching long flat elastic bands around ankle height from both sides, hopping in between; morning light) (3) Shade beneath the water tower (4) Curb in front of the community center (cat's cradle game using a looped string around hands; sunbeams) (5) Park sandbox (mud dumplings: spheres made of mud covered in dry sand and polished shiny by hand; white light) (6) In front of mailboxes (evening orange light) (7) Complex stairs (evening). No signs or lettering on screen. Do not display address details on envelopes.

[Camera] Aesthetics of a 1986 home video camera: bleeding colors, low resolution, blown-out bright skies, soft outlines. No date stamps. Handheld with realistic shaking, imperfect framework, hesitant zooming, shifting exposure. Distance of 2 to 5 meters from the subject. The subject disregards the camera. No stabilization, gimbals, drones, slow motion, cinematic setup, or commercial color grading. The camera is always recorded from the physical position held by the operator (standing, sitting, crouching, walking, next seat). Avoid perspectives from impossible locations (mid-air, underwater, ceiling, directly above, outside running vehicles, centimeters from the face). The operator acts as an actual person sharing the environment, tracking with a short delay when the subject moves, sometimes losing ideal framing.

[Shots] (approx. 2 seconds each. Each line = location/light / focus / internal emotion expressed via subtle motions / camera position)
1. Balcony, morning. Weaving through drying laundry while adjusting her red hair clip. Emotion: motivated. Clamping mouth shut while pushing the pin in. Camera: from the inside looking out, sheets glowing white in backlight.
2. Courtyard, elastics game. Jumping the elastics, catching her foot and nearly falling, laughing spontaneously. Emotion: fully immersed and happy. Camera: front view, waist height, slightly back.
3. Shadow of the water tower. Three girls sitting together, drinking barley tea from a thermos cup. Looking at the far sky with the cup pressed to her mouth before passing it to the next child. Emotion: hot but relieved. Camera: side view.
4. Curb in front of the community center, sunbeams. Completing the "ladder" pattern in cat's cradle, staring at her hands and smiling. Emotion: satisfied with success. Camera: oblique front angle, focusing on hands.
5. Sandbox. Enfolding a polished mud dumpling in both hands, tilting it against the light to look at angles. Emotion: proud. Sparkling eyes. Camera: crouching close to the mud dumpling.
6. In front of mailboxes, evening. Standing on tiptoes to peer inside, pulling out an envelope (plain, hiding addresses) and cradling it against her chest. Emotion: excited anticipation. Camera: side view.
7. Complex stairs, evening. Back view of her running up holding the envelope. Turning past the landing out of sight. Emotion: eager to share. Camera: looking up from the base of the stairs. Around 00:14, the video cuts abruptly to a black screen. No fade-out.

[Item/Prop Details] The elastic string is a white, flat, wide band. The thermos is red plastic with a lid that acts as a cup. Mud dumplings are shiny dark brown. Cat's cradle string is a loop of red yarn. The envelope is plain white. The red pin is plastic with a round top.

[Text Prohibition] No legible text, logos, signs, labels, or numbers on screen. The envelope is blank.

[Physics/Consistency] Real-world physics. No excess digits, fused limbs, warped anatomy, floating items, vanishing objects, or sudden transformations. Feet touch the ground properly. Red pin, jumper skirt, and friends' apparel stay uniform across all scenes.

[Audio] Natural environmental sounds only (cutting with each shot): flapping laundry, foot thuds and laughter from elastics play, thermos noises, birds in sunbeams, sand shuffling, metallic mailbox clicks, steps on stairs. No spoken dialogue. Only occasional low giggles/breathing from the camerawork operator or subject allowed. No music. No narration. No synthetic sound production effects.

[Atmosphere] Replicating a simple day for a Showa-era girl that makes adults think "I used to do that." Fragments of standard play and tasks over simulated acting. Nostalgic, endearing, deeply human. Prioritize a random, organic camera presence.

promptText:

SHOT 1 (00:00-00:03.5) Opening Display

SHOT 4 (00:09.5-00:13) Second slide + Click instant change

SHOT 5 (00:13-00:16.5) Third slide + Click instant change

[Director Rules]
1. Transition Rule: Each change must occur on the same frame as the 'click', instant single-frame change. Character position, pose, hairstyle, and face shape must be perfectly continuous across the transition frame.
2. POV Rule: Camera = male lead's eyes, slight handheld breathing shake throughout; male lead only shows hands + voiceover, no face.

Negative: Dissolve changes, black frames, white flashes, smoke, spinning transitions, character teleporting, posture breakage, facial changes, hairstyle changes, shoe changes (unless in outfit image), male lead face reveal, horizontal screen, subtitles, watermarks, logos, sudden background change, extra people, baggy home clothes unless in the asset, heavy camera shake, unreadable screen.

title: Hollywood Disaster Action Storyboard
description: A high-intensity 30-second survival sequence set in Kuala Lumpur, featuring realistic building collapses, vehicle chaos, and continuous character action.
promptText:
TITLE: THE SURVIVAL RUN

Create a single-page, premium Hollywood disaster-action storyboard in 16:9 widescreen format with 12 cinematic panels covering one continuous 30-second survival sequence.

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 (Image1):
Use as the EXACT main character reference. Maintain the same facial identity, hairstyle, beard, body proportions, black shirt, black pants and overall appearance consistently in every panel. No character, face, hairstyle or clothing changes. Dust and debris may gradually appear as the disaster progresses.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 (Image2):
Use as the EXACT storyboard design and layout reference. Match its premium cinematic panel arrangement, numbering, timecodes, black caption strips, typography hierarchy, borders and professional Hollywood storyboard presentation.

STYLE:
Photorealistic live-action Hollywood disaster film, ARRI Alexa 35, anamorphic cinematic lens, realistic Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, practical stunt realism, believable destruction physics, handheld tracking, cinematic lighting, motion blur, dust, shattered glass, sparks and realistic debris.

CORE RULE:
ONE CONTINUOUS SURVIVAL SHOT. Every movement must logically connect. No teleportation or unexplained location changes. The same man constantly runs, stumbles, recovers, jumps, slides and changes direction while the collapsing city becomes the antagonist.

STORYBOARD PANELS:

1. 00:00–00:03 — EARTHQUAKE
Low-angle behind his feet as he runs through Kuala Lumpur. The ground shakes, buildings tremble, glass explodes and concrete crashes behind him. He looks back and accelerates.

2. 00:03–00:06 — COLLAPSE
Front tracking shot. A building façade collapses behind him. He changes direction and jumps over a metal barrier as debris destroys his original path.

3. 00:06–00:09 — CAR IMPACT
At an intersection, vehicles slide toward him. He dives at the last second, a car passes overhead, he rolls, recovers and keeps running.

4. 00:09–00:12 — ROAD CRACK
A huge fissure tears across the road. He runs onto a damaged car as a springboard and leaps across collapsing pavement.

5. 00:12–00:15 — FALLING GLASS
Side tracking shot. High-rise windows explode above him. Glass rains down as he shields his face and ducks beneath a falling sign.

6. 00:15–00:18 — COLLAPSE
A building collapses ahead. He spots a narrow gap, drops low and slides beneath falling debris, then emerges dusty and runs.

7. 00:18–00:21 — VEHICLE CHAOS
A bus crashes into cars. A spinning vehicle approaches. He jumps onto its hood, springs over the roof and lands on the opposite sidewalk.

8. 00:21–00:24 — ELEVATED ROAD FAILURE
An elevated road collapses ahead. He performs a desperate full-body gap jump, lands hard, rolls, recovers and runs.
